purpose: The same table joined twice in different roles (nation as supplier and customer nation)
sql:
SELECT sn.n_name AS supplier_nation, cn.n_name AS customer_nation, count(*) AS line_count
FROM lineitem l
JOIN supplier s  ON s.s_suppkey = l.l_suppkey
JOIN orders o    ON o.o_orderkey = l.l_orderkey
JOIN customer c  ON c.c_custkey = o.o_custkey
JOIN nation sn   ON sn.n_nationkey = s.s_nationkey
JOIN nation cn   ON cn.n_nationkey = c.c_nationkey
WHERE sn.n_name = 'JAPAN'
  AND cn.n_name = 'BRAZIL'
  AND l.l_shipdate BETWEEN DATE '1995-01-01' AND DATE '1995-03-31'
GROUP BY sn.n_name, cn.n_name

extra.AI Reason: Aggregating the joined result set by nation names.
Joining filtered orders with filtered customers.
Joining filtered lineitems with suppliers from Japan.
Scanning lineitem for date range filter.

join_order.postgres: HJ(NL(HJ(orders, HJ(customer, nation)), lineitem), HJ(supplier, nation))
join_order.ai: HJ(HJ(HJ(lineitem, HJ(supplier, nation)), orders), HJ(customer, nation))

differences.text: The join order differs. PostgreSQL builds the intermediate result(s) {customer, lineitem, nation, orders}; {customer, nation, orders}, which the AI plan does not. The AI builds {lineitem, nation, orders, supplier}; {lineitem, nation, supplier}, which PostgreSQL does not. This changes the size of every intermediate result.
PostgreSQL runs part of the plan in parallel (Gather), with partial aggregation in each worker. The AI plan runs in a single process.

Aggregate (Sorted, Finalize) over (orders, customer, nation, lineitem, supplier, nation): PostgreSQL uses Sorted aggregation, the AI uses Hashed. Hashed aggregation needs no sorted input but more memory. Sorted aggregation needs sorted input but little memory. The AI's reason: "Aggregating the joined result set by nation names."

Hash Join of (orders, customer, nation, lineitem) with (supplier, nation): PostgreSQL applies l_suppkey = s_suppkey here, the AI does not. The AI applies o_custkey = c_custkey here, PostgreSQL does not.

Table lineitem: PostgreSQL uses Index Scan on lineitem using lineitem_pkey. The AI uses Seq Scan on lineitem. A sequential scan wins when many rows qualify. An index scan wins when few rows qualify. A bitmap scan sits in between. The AI's reason: "Scanning lineitem for date range filter."
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Gather over (orders, customer, nation, lineitem, supplier, nation) (collects rows from parallel worker processes).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Aggregate (Sorted, Partial) over (orders, customer, nation, lineitem, supplier, nation) (computes aggregates (GROUP BY, SUM, COUNT, ...)).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Nested Loop of (orders, customer, nation) with (lineitem) (for every outer row, searches the inner input for matches).
Only the PostgreSQL plan has Hash Join of (orders) with (customer, nation) (builds a hash table on the inner input, then probes it with every outer row).

Only the AI plan has Hash Join of (lineitem, supplier, nation) with (orders) (builds a hash table on the inner input, then probes it with every outer row). The AI's reason: "Joining filtered lineitems with orders."

Only the AI plan has Hash Join of (lineitem) with (supplier, nation) (builds a hash table on the inner input, then probes it with every outer row). The AI's reason: "Joining filtered lineitems with suppliers from Japan."
Only the AI plan has Hash over (orders) (builds the in-memory hash table for a Hash Join). The AI's reason: "Hashing orders."
